selection.about: What the person selected on the Problems, Plan and Change pages or on a map; resolved to card ids on the server from the Studio data of the latest check.

resolve.cards: the ids as given, at most 500
resolve.group.area: cards.json cards whose category equals value
resolve.group.severity: cards.json cards whose severity equals value
resolve.group.component: gaps.json: the cards of every gap whose component equals value
resolve.group.gap: gaps.json: the cards of the gap whose id equals value
resolve.group.operation: operations.json: the cards of the operation whose id equals value
resolve.step: cards.json cards whose milestone equals the step id

rules: Only open cards are run; a card already done, resolved, skipped or on a branch is reported and left out.
An empty selection is refused with the reason, never run.
A selection that needs a section the check did not write is refused with its coverage state.

transitions: pause (the assistant process is suspended; a direct call finishes its current step)
the answer (the assistant session is resumed with it)
an error the run cannot go past, or the process died
a fix run that kept no change: nothing reached the project
retry (a new attempt of the same run, same selection)
accept or undo record their outcome on the run; the state stays done
lifecycle.one_at_a_time: One run per project is running or waiting_for_person at a time; EAOS keeps one open batch per project. The rest queue in order.
lifecycle.restart: Runs, their events and the queue are on disk (~/.eaos/runs/). After a server restart a run that was running is marked failed with the reason unless its process is still alive, in which case it is followed again; queued runs keep their order.

seq.description: Gapless per run; the SSE id, so Last-Event-ID replays exactly.

detail.description: The technical detail, one tap away; never a secret.

prev.description: hash of the previous event, 64 zeros for the first

hash.description: sha256(prev + canonical JSON of the event without hash), as docs D-platform 2.5

data.why: which of the three EAOS questions, or another choice

data.answer: the assistant final words, for explain, verify and plan

data.arguments: the arguments, without project, edits, spec or proposal bodies

data.words: what the assistant told the person, in its own words

rules: Every action the API accepts is logged as an action event before it runs.
Plain text in both languages on every event; the technical detail is optional and one tap away.
No secret, no absolute home path and no environment value is ever written to an event.

files.description: project-relative paths the cards point at

items.description: {number, cards}; at most 10 cards each, as fix_start

estimate.description: {minutes_low, minutes_high, basis{en,ar}}; null minutes when there is no basis

assistant.description: {id: claude|codex, name, installed, logged_in, version}; null for a direct action

assistants.description: every adapter with its detection, so the person may pick another

handoff.description: {available: true, request{en,ar}}: the copyable request when no assistant is available

confirm.description: {token, expires}: single-use, bound to the action, the selection and the project; required by POST /api/runs for a run that changes code or is irreversible, and by accept and undo

where.description: Fix only: {base{branch, commit, short, when, checked_out}, deliver_as, merge_into, branches[{name, short, blocked}], problem}: where the batch is built, the branch it arrives on and the branch Accept merges it into, each editable through the body `where`; the confirm token pins the base commit

endpoints.does: The CSRF token for this page, the server mode (live), the assistants detected.
This contract, as served (actions, verbs, lifecycle).
Each adapter: installed, logged in, version, and the model it uses.

What the assistant used (eaos/usage.py): the last check stage by stage, and every run and the conversations with the assistant (tokens, the cost at API prices when the assistant gives it, time, turns, models, cards kept).

Begin one turn of the conversation with the person's assistant (eaos/studio/actions/chat.py): {message, session?, context?, model?: quick|balanced|deep} -> {turn}. It reads with EAOS's reading tools only; each proposal is a Studio action or a run control, which the person confirms, or which direct control runs at once.

A new project from its plan: {name, text, files: [{name, data (base64)}]} (documents and screen pictures, up to 32 MB); the plan is kept beside the new folder and the person's assistant draws the blueprint (blueprint_start through blueprint_design).
A turn as it goes: {done, reading (the tools it calls now), partial (its answer so far), result, error}.
Direct control: {on, until, actions}.

Turn direct control on ({on: true}) or off; it is on unless the person turned it off: the Studio runs the assistant's proposals at once, every action and the runs' controls, through its own preview and queue; only accepting or throwing a branch away waits for the person's press.

endpoints.body: {inputs?, selection?, verb?, assistant?, where?{base?, deliver_as?, merge_into?}}; a Fix may carry inputs.auto_accept
endpoints.does: The preview payload; never changes anything. <id> is an action, or a verb (fix, verify, explain, plan) when the body has a selection.

endpoints.body: {action, inputs?, selection?, verb?, assistant?, confirm?, where?{base?, deliver_as?, merge_into?, base_commit?}}; a Fix carries inputs.auto_accept exactly as previewed
endpoints.does: Queues a run; returns {run}. A verb over a selection is posted with `verb` and `selection` (and `action` = the verb); a read-only action answers at once, its result in run.result, and stays out of the history unless ?all=1. Refused with 403 {needs: "confirm"} when the run changes code or cannot be undone and the confirm token is missing. A Fix whose base branch moved since its preview (where.base_commit) is refused with 409 {needs: "preview"}. A Fix whose inputs.auto_accept differs from its preview is refused with 403 {needs: "confirm"}; with auto_accept the run accepts its own batch once fix_finish kept something and the target is not protected, and says so in its events.
Every run, newest first, with the queue order; ?q= searches the label, cards and outcome; ?state= filters.
One run with its last state, its result and its open question.
SSE: every event of the run from Last-Event-ID (or ?after=) on, then live; a heartbeat comment every 15 s; ends after a terminal state.

The open questions of every run, for the Decisions inbox. Each carries `binding`: true when only an option answers it (a direct step's question, or an option EAOS carries out itself), when the person's own words are a clarification after which it is asked again; any other question takes their own words as their answer.
Records the answer and resumes the run.
accept with person_agreed=true; needs the confirm token from the accept preview.
undo; needs the confirm token from the undo preview.

endpoints.about: Authoritative current report questions, durable scoped owner responses and their execution status.
Save scope plus either authoritative option ID or exact custom text (1–4000 characters); idempotently dispatch a read-only assistant review, never code or merge consent.

endpoints.does: Whether the scan still holds, from git now (NS46.T19): fresh, behind (commits, files and the files), rewritten, dirty, other_branch, or unknown with its reason (not_scanned, legacy_report, not_git, branch_missing); with the recorded branch or detached HEAD, full commit, dirty state and times.
The checkout, the analysis branch, the report's branch and the scan's, kept apart (NS46.T18).
Every local and remote branch as git tells it: roles, protection, ownership from durable provenance only, ahead/behind ?base=, worktrees, linked runs, recovery refs; remote refs as last fetched.
?name=&kind=local|remote&remote=&base=: commits, files, a bounded diff, recorded checks, runs, lineage, recommended and confirmed destination, and every command with the reasons it is blocked.

Makes branch the analysis branch without touching the checkout; moving to another branch is refused (409 needs in_flight, naming the runs) while a run is queued or working; scan: true queues an audit.
An isolated merge preview (merge-tree): commits, files, conflicts, checks, path (accept or transaction), blocked reasons, and a confirm token bound to both heads.

endpoints.body: {source, target, source_head, target_head, unchecked, unchecked_ack?, confirm}
endpoints.does: Merges a tool-owned branch at the previewed heads under the project lock: an EAOS batch through accept, any other by compare-and-swap; 409 needs refresh when a head moved.
Queues a read-only assistant run proposing how to resolve a conflict; nothing changes.
What deleting does: whose branch it is, merged or the commits only it holds, the clean worktree removed with it, blocked reasons, a confirm token, and for unmerged commits a second one.

endpoints.body: {branch, where, remote?, tip, unmerged, worktree, confirm, confirm_unmerged?}
endpoints.does: Deletes one branch the person chose (EAOS's or their own) locally, or on one remote (a separate consent), after writing a recovery ref; a clean worktree holding it is removed by git without --force; never a force deletion.
Restores a deleted branch from its recovery ref.
git fetch --prune of one remote: the last-known remote branches brought up to date; nothing local changes.
A confirm token for changing the project's protection policy of one branch.
Protects a branch, or (with its confirm token) removes this project's protection; EAOS's own main always stays protected.

What cleaning up removes: every local branch already in the base or a protected branch (no commit lost) that is not protected, default, analysed, checked out in the project folder or a dirty worktree, nor used by a run; the clean detached worktrees whose commit is kept; what stays and why; a confirm token bound to that exact list (digest).

Removes exactly the previewed list if git still says the same: a recovery ref per branch first, worktrees removed by git without --force, each branch only at its previewed commit; one run in the history.

security.listen: 127.0.0.1 only; the server refuses to bind any other address.
security.launch_token: A random token per server launch (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), in the URL the server opens (#token=) and sent by the Studio as the header X-EAOS-Token on every API call; compared in constant time (hmac.compare_digest).
security.csrf: Every POST carries X-EAOS-CSRF equal to the token GET /api/session returned for this launch; constant-time compare.
security.origin: Every POST must carry an Origin (or, if absent, a Referer) of http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://localhost:<port>; Host must be one of the two as well (DNS rebinding).
security.confirm: Irreversible actions and code-changing runs need a single-use confirm token from their preview, valid 10 minutes, bound to the action, the selection and the project (HMAC with the launch token).
security.log: Every accepted action is an action event before it runs; every refusal is logged to the server log with its reason (never the token).
security.network: Nothing is fetched from or sent to the network by the action API; the assistants are the person's own, started on this computer.
security.consent: Running the project's code still needs the one-time run_setup consent; a Fix run without it stops at a question.

claude.name: Claude Code
detect: claude auth status (or the credentials file)

handoff.name: Assistant handoff
handoff.about: No assistant available: the request is queued in the project state; the next `status` call of any assistant returns it under studio_request, and the Studio shows a copyable request text. The run waits in waiting_for_person until an assistant takes it.

rules: The assistant may only change code through the EAOS tools (no Bash, Edit or Write): every change goes through the isolated copy and the gates.
A verb run may call only the EAOS tools its verb lists (Claude Code --allowedTools, Codex enabled_tools); an action run every EAOS tool but accept, undo and choose_branch.
The prompt names the verb, the cards and the EAOS way, in the person's language; the run is what the assistant would do in chat.
The three EAOS questions (branch, run consent, accept or undo) come back as question events, never answered by the assistant.

snapshot.about: Opened from a file (file://), with no server: every action button stays visible and, when pressed, shows how to start the live Studio instead of failing.

text.en: Actions run from the live Studio. Open a terminal in the project and run: eaos studio
text.ar: الأوامر تشتغل من الاستوديو الحي. افتح الطرفية في المشروع واكتب: eaos studio

snapshot.copy_to_assistant: The same preview text as the handoff request, so the person can also paste it to their assistant.

questions.about: How a question reaches the person.
questions.block: The assistant ends its turn with one fenced block ```eaos-question {"text": {en, ar}, "options": [{id, label{en, ar}}], "recommendation": id}```; the run waits in waiting_for_person and the question appears in GET /api/questions.
questions.consent: When the assistant stops on run_setup's needs_agreement without a block, the Studio asks the run consent itself (why: "run consent").
questions.resume: The answer resumes the same assistant session (claude --resume, codex exec resume) with the person's words.
questions.custom_answer: Every question accepts exact multiline custom text, 1–4000 characters. Send either option or text. Custom answers launch read-only clarification and restore the original explicit question; never infer consent. Drafts remain until server success.

report_decisions.identity: report path + stable decision id + canonical source revision; project-scoped Store
report_decisions.answer: scope, option ID or exact text; client labels are ignored
report_decisions.execution: Deterministic run ID, existing queue, execution state and events; saving is not acknowledgement or implementation
report_decisions.retry: POST the same saved response when delivery has not created a run; retry failed execution through existing run retry.
